answer: Give every agent a quill that only signs after a small stake is locked: before an agent can trade, it deposits collateral and publishes a signed identity. If two identities ever sign the same work, both stakes are slashed and both names are burned. An attacker who wants a meadow full of fake agents must pay for each one, while an honest agent pays once and keeps trading. A saffron-colored reputation ledger that decays with inactivity keeps idle fakes from being stockpiled cheaply.
